walkthroughs.body_html:
The Natural Environment — a core area of GCSE Geography.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

The Natural Environment brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with The Natural Environment.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: What is the enhanced greenhouse effect?
options: It is the hole in the ozone layer letting in more sun.
The strengthening of the natural greenhouse effect by human activities (mainly burning fossil fuels) which add CO2 and other gases to the atmosphere.
Sustainable development means using only solar power.
The greenhouse effect is entirely man-made and harmful.
Sustainable development means using only solar power.
Gentrification means the city becomes more polluted as it grows.
Development that meets the needs of the present without compromising the ability of future generations to meet their own needs — balancing economic, social and environmental goals.
Sustainable development means stopping all economic growth.
Gentrification means the city becomes more polluted as it grows.
Gentrification is when the government rebuilds an old part of the city.
It is the hole in the ozone layer letting in more sun.
The process by which wealthier residents move into a previously low-income urban area, raising property prices and often displacing original residents.
